CONTRACTS9 September 20267 min read

Employment pre-contracts: what they commit you to and what to define.

Where a hire depends on a date, authorisation or project confirmation, a pre-contract can document the commitment. It must be drafted precisely.

KEY POINT

Calling a document a “pre-contract” does not stop it creating obligations. Content, consent and specificity matter.All resources ↗

Where a hire depends on a date, authorisation or project confirmation, a pre-contract can document the commitment. It must be drafted precisely.

01

Who makes the commitment

The organisation and future worker must be identified, and the signatory must have sufficient authority.

02

Which role or activity is offered

Duties, category, location and responsibilities should be defined to avoid incompatible interpretations.

03

When the person is expected to start

State a date or objective criterion and clearly express any future condition on which hiring depends.

04

Which essential terms are agreed

Contract type, hours, duration, pay and collective agreement help define the commitment.

05

What happens if it cannot proceed

Conditions, deadlines and grounds for ending the agreement should be drafted carefully.

Practical review

Offer, pre-contract and employment contract

  • An offer proposes terms; whether acceptance is binding must be assessed.
  • A pre-contract records a future hiring commitment to the extent of its content.
  • An employment contract governs the actual work and its conditions.
Legislative sourceBOE · Official consolidated text

Information updated on 9 September 2026. Effects depend on each document’s content and circumstances.
